summary.intent: Update the codebase map documents (primarily CONCERNS.md, and STRUCTURE.md) to reflect the completed work in phases 28-33, then commit and PR the changes.
summary.outcome: CONCERNS.md (233 lines) and STRUCTURE.md (565 lines) were updated via parallel mapper agents, committed on a docs branch, and a PR was opened (FSM1/cipher-box#390). A stale POC concern was also manually corrected after the user caught it.

repo: Phase 28 replaced all 127 console.* calls with a structured logger at apps/web/src/lib/logger.ts, but web3auth/hooks.ts retained 12 console.time/timeEnd calls outside the logger.
Phase 30 added Grafana Faro observability (apps/web/src/lib/faro.ts), but registerFaroTransport() was defined and never called, meaning logger.error/warn calls don't reach Faro.
Phase 31 decomposed useSharedNavigation.ts (1199→378 lines) and FileBrowser.tsx (964→362 lines); remaining large files folder.service.ts (1059) and bin.service.ts (971) are now considered acceptable.

Phase 32 (macOS) and Phase 33 (Windows) both resolved the sync FilePointer blocking concern — crates/fuse/src/read_ops.rs and crates/fuse/src/platform/windows/read_ops.rs now use async resolution via rt.spawn() channel patterns.
The legacy POC directory was removed in commit ee9bcd4e4 during Phase 28, but the codebase map still listed it as a concern — the map had stale data.
19+ mutex lock().unwrap() sites exist in FUSE production code, creating a cascading panic risk on poisoned mutexes.
IPNS unenrollment is fire-and-forget with no persistence across tab closure.

workflow: When origin has new commits and local has diverged, stash specific files, reset to origin/main, then restore — avoids a messy merge of planning docs.
Re-running mapper agents after pulling latest (Phase 33 merged) produced more accurate results than the first run against the pre-pull state.
Mapper agents write documents directly and return only confirmations, keeping orchestrator context usage minimal.
The codebase map can silently go stale — manual review after agents complete is important to catch cases like the POC concern.

friction: git pull failed with divergent branches error because the codebase map commit had been made locally before pulling Phase 33 — required a manual stash/reset/restore dance.
The first concerns mapping run was done against pre-Phase-33 state, so the whole agent had to be re-run after pulling latest main.
The mapper agent missed that the legacy POC concern was stale (removed in Phase 28) — required user to catch it manually post-PR.
